source: Tool names and input schemas: SynapCores CE gateway, POST /v1/mcp tools/list (2.4.8). Titles, descriptions, parameter descriptions and annotations rewritten 2026-11-20 against the 2.5.1 gateway implementation (crates/aidb-gateway/src/routes/mcp/tools.rs).

tools.name: describe_table
tools.title: Describe a table's columns
tools.description: Return the column definitions of one table: name, type, nullable, primary_key and default for each column. Use it before writing INSERT/UPDATE statements or WHERE filters, once `list_tables` has given you the table name; it reads the schema, not the data, unless include_samples=true, which adds up to 5 distinct example values per column (one SELECT DISTINCT per column).

database.description: Database name; omit to use the default database.

include_samples.description: true = add up to 5 distinct sample values per column (default false).

tools.name: execute
tools.title: Run a SQL write or schema change
tools.description: Run a SQL write (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) or schema change (CREATE, ALTER, DROP) against a SynapCores database and return rows_affected and execution_time_ms. Use `query` for SELECT/WITH, which this tool rejects, and `validate_query` or dry_run=true to check syntax without changing anything; Cypher statements sent here run on the graph, as with `graph_query`. Changes are permanent (DELETE and DROP remove data), and read-only API keys are refused.

sql.description: The INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, ALTER or DROP statement to run.

database.description: Database name; omit to use the default database.

dry_run.description: true = only check the syntax and change nothing (default false).

tools.name: list_tables
tools.title: List tables
tools.description: List the tables in a SynapCores database, optionally filtered by a LIKE-style name pattern, and return {database, tables: [{name}], count}. Use it to discover what exists before writing SQL; use `describe_table` for a table's columns and types. Internal tables (names starting with "_") are hidden unless include_system=true. Read-only.

database.description: Database name; omit to use the default database.

pattern.description: Name filter with LIKE wildcards: % matches any run of characters, _ matches one character (for example 'order%').

include_system.description: true = also list internal tables whose names start with '_' (default false).

tools.name: query
tools.title: Run a read-only SQL query
tools.description: Run a read-only SQL SELECT (or WITH ... SELECT) on a SynapCores database and return the rows. Use it to read data, including vector search over table columns with EMBED() and COSINE_SIMILARITY(); use `execute` for writes and schema changes (any other statement is rejected here), `graph_query` for Cypher, and `semantic_search` for vector collections. When the SQL has no LIMIT, LIMIT `limit` (default 1000, max 10000) and OFFSET `offset` are appended. Returns column names and types plus rows as JSON, or a Markdown table or CSV per `format`.

sql.description: A SELECT or WITH statement. Look up syntax and AI functions with `sql_manual`.

database.description: Database name; omit to use the default database.

limit.description: Row cap appended as LIMIT when the SQL has none (default 1000, max 10000).

offset.description: Rows to skip, appended as OFFSET (default 0); combine with `limit` to page through results.

format.description: rows = JSON with columns and rows (default); markdown = a table; csv = comma-separated text.

tools.name: sql_manual
tools.title: SynapCores SQL reference
tools.description: Look up SynapCores SQL syntax and examples for one topic (for example SELECT, CREATE TABLE, EMBED, COSINE_SIMILARITY or ASK), or browse a whole category. Use it before writing SQL for `query` or `execute`, especially SynapCores-specific AI functions; it reads built-in documentation only and never touches your data. An unknown topic returns an error listing topics you can use.

topic.description: Statement or function to look up, for example 'SELECT', 'CREATE TABLE', 'EMBED' or 'COSINE_SIMILARITY'.

category.description: Browse a whole category instead of one topic: statements, functions, operators, types or all (default all).

tools.name: validate_query
tools.title: Check SQL without running it
tools.description: Check whether a SQL statement parses, without running it, and return {valid, statement_type, errors}. With include_plan=true, a SELECT also returns its execution plan (EXPLAIN), which helps spot slow queries. Use it before `execute` on writes you want to be sure of, or to debug a failing `query`; it never changes data.

sql.description: The SQL statement to check (any statement type).

include_plan.description: true = also return the execution plan; applies to SELECT statements (default false).

tools.name: train_model
tools.title: Train an AutoML model
tools.description: Train an AutoML model that predicts one column of a table from its other columns, without writing SQL: wraps CREATE EXPERIMENT, runs `max_trials` trials, keeps the best algorithm, registers it as `model_name`, and returns the best score (accuracy for classification, R² for regression) and the algorithm. Then call `predict` with that name, or `describe_model` for full metrics. Reusing an existing `model_name` replaces that model; more trials take longer and can score higher. Table, target and feature names must use only letters, digits and underscores.

collection.description: Table that holds the training rows.

features.description: Columns to learn from; omit or leave empty to use every column except `target`.

task_type.description: binary_classification (default), multiclass_classification, regression, or classification (treated as binary).

max_trials.description: How many AutoML trials to run (default 3); more trials take longer and can find a better model.

model_name.description: Name to register the model under (default {collection}_{target}_model); an existing model with this name is replaced.

tools.name: predict
tools.title: Predict with a trained model
tools.description: Score rows with a model trained by `train_model` and return {predictions, model_name, latency_ms, row_count}: calibrated probabilities in [0, 1] for classification (positive-class probability) or numbers for regression, one per input row. Use it for inference on rows you pass inline; use `describe_model` to check a model's metrics and features first. Every row must have the same columns, named like the training columns. Your tables are not modified.

model_name.description: Model name, as registered by `train_model` or listed by `list_models`.

inputs.description: Rows to score, as objects mapping column names to values, e.g. [{"col1": 1, "col2": "a"}]; all rows need the same columns.

return_proba.description: Accepted for compatibility; classification models always return calibrated probabilities.

tools.name: list_models
tools.title: List AutoML models
tools.description: List the AutoML models this tenant has trained, filtered by status (default deployed) and optionally task type, and return {models: [{name, task_type, status, version, created_at}], count}. Use it to find a model name for `predict`; use `describe_model` for accuracy, hyperparameters and feature importance. Read-only.

task_type.description: Only return models of this task type, e.g. binary_classification or regression.

status.description: Only return models with this status (default deployed).

tools.name: describe_model
tools.title: Describe an AutoML model
tools.description: Get full details of one trained AutoML model: algorithm, hyperparameters, metrics, feature names, and feature importance when the algorithm provides it. Use it after `list_models` or `train_model` to judge a model before relying on `predict`. Read-only.

model_name.description: Model name, as registered by `train_model` or listed by `list_models`.

include_feature_importance.description: true = include per-feature importance scores (default true).

tools.name: semantic_search
tools.title: Semantic search in a vector collection
tools.description: Find the k items in a vector collection closest in meaning to a natural-language query: the tool embeds `query_text` with the engine's configured embedding model, searches the collection, and returns {results: [{id, similarity, metadata}], count, collection}. Use it for vector collections; for vectors stored in SQL table columns, use `query` with EMBED() and COSINE_SIMILARITY(). `filter` keeps only results whose metadata equals the given values and is applied after the top-k search, so fewer than k results can come back. Read-only.

collection.description: Name of the vector collection to search.

query_text.description: Natural-language text to search for; it is embedded for you.

k.description: Number of nearest matches to return (default 10, max 1000).

filter.description: Metadata values results must equal, e.g. {"category": "electronics"}; applied after the top-k search.

tools.name: embed_text
tools.title: Embed text as a vector
tools.description: Turn a piece of text into an embedding vector with the engine's configured embedding model and return {embedding, dimensions, model}. Use it when you need the raw vector, for example to store it or compare it yourself; to search, use `semantic_search` for vector collections or `query` with EMBED() and COSINE_SIMILARITY() for table columns. Nothing is stored.

text.description: Text to embed, such as a sentence or short passage.

model.description: Accepted for compatibility; the engine always uses its configured embedding model, reported in the response's `model` field.

tools.name: graph_query
tools.title: Run a Cypher graph query
tools.description: Run Cypher against a database's property graph and return {rows, execution_time_ms}: read with MATCH, write with CREATE, MERGE, SET and DELETE, combine with UNWIND and UNION, and run graph algorithms with `CALL gds.<algorithm>(...) YIELD ...`; separate several statements with `;`. Use it for relationship questions such as paths, neighbors and communities; use `query` for SQL tables. Write clauses change the graph permanently, and read-only API keys are refused for them.

database.description: Database whose graph to use (default main).

cypher.description: Cypher text with literal values written inline; separate multiple statements with `;`.

params.description: Not used for binding; write values inline in `cypher`.

graph_name.description: Reserved; queries always run on the selected database's graph.

tools.name: generate_text
tools.title: Generate text with the engine's LLM
tools.description: Generate text from a prompt with the LLM configured on the SynapCores engine and return {text, model, tokens_used, processing_time_ms}. Use it to summarize or explain results from other tools, such as `predict` or `query` output, inside a multi-step workflow; to generate per row inside SQL, use GENERATE() in `query`. It does not read or change your data, and output is sampled, so repeated calls can differ.

model.description: Model name to use instead of the engine's configured completion model.

max_tokens.description: Maximum tokens to generate (default 100); raise it for longer answers.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature; lower is more focused (default 0.7).

tools.name: agent_soul
tools.title: Inspect an agent's learned state
tools.description: Inspect the current tenant/database's learned memory, episodes, rewards, runs, plans, goals, skills, policy or audit, one section per call. Use it to review or audit what an agent has learned and why it acts as it does; use `query` for ordinary SQL tables. Administrator required; read-only, paginated, no execution.

database.description: Database whose agent state to inspect.

after.description: Pagination cursor from the previous page; omit for the first page.
